sentences.text: The genus Archaeogaleus contains only one known species, A. lengadocensis.
The species name lengadocensis refers to the historical Occitan-speaking region of Lengadòc.
The genus Archaeogaleus was described by Guinot, Cappetta, and Adnet in 2014.
Archaeogaleus was first described from fossils found in the Valanginian stage of France.
Archaeogaleus is the oldest known requiem shark.
Archaeogaleus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks.
Archaeogaleus belongs to the parent group Carcharhinidae.
Archaeogaleus lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
